notes:
Unified-rule spec (scenario-meanings.md#background-subagent) for Hermes. Hermes' subagent primitive is `delegate_task`, and a top-level delegation is background BY CONSTRUCTION - _model_background_value (delegate_tool.py:3642-3655) forces background for every call the top-level agent makes and the schema's `background` field is documented DEPRECATED/IGNORED - so the tool returns a handle immediately ("{n} subagents are running in parallel in the background", delegate_tool.py:3070), the parent finishes its own reply ('dispatched'), and the consolidated batch result re-enters as a NEW turn after every child drains (async_delegation.py: completion_queue, drained by the CLI process_loop while idle). That is 3.2's defining ordering: the parent's end_turn lands BEFORE the child drain. Birth is modelled in TWO phases because hermes declares a ProcessMatcher: processlifecycle mints a transient proc-<PID> presession at launch while the real sessions row (id shaped YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_<hex6>) is INSERTed ~2s later on the first user message. NO LONGER KNOWN_FAILING - re-assessed at commit 6ad7c28a. Hermes persists each delegate child as its own sessions row with parent_session_id = the parent's id (run_agent.py:606-640 _ensure_db_session, with session_db + parent_session_id injected at delegate_tool.py:1390-1391), tagged source='subagent' (platform="subagent" at delegate_tool.py:1385 -> _session_source_for_agent's platform fallback, run_agent.py:92-102). The adapter's allow-list previously read `source IN ('cli','tui')` and dropped that row; both query sites now read `source IN ('cli','tui','subagent')` (watcher.go:284, metrics.go:103), so the child surfaces carrying the ParentSessionID the watcher already resolves (watcher.go:281,378). From there the machinery is agent-agnostic and keyed only on ParentSessionID: indexParentChildren/ComputeSubagentSummary (grouped.go:90-106,266-300) count the live child, hasActiveChildren (session_detector_subagent.go:206-221) holds the parent working across its own end_turn, and reevaluateParent releases it only after the last child drains. FAITHFULNESS GATE: child_link must precede child_drain, and the parent must NOT go ready between child_link and child_drain (the held_working invariant) - if the parent went ready while a child was alive that is a daemon regression; if the parent only went ready AFTER blocking on the children inline that would be a foreground clone, which hermes cannot produce (there is no synchronous delegation - see the sibling 3.1 cell, agent=no). Two hermes-specific notes for whoever reads a failure: SubagentQuietWindow is NOT in play (isOrphanedChild os.Stats "<store>?session=<id>", the stat fails, so no child is ever fast-forwarded), and the child sharing the parent's PID is safe (assignPIDLocked exempts ParentSessionID != "" from same-PID cleanup, pid_manager.go:622-652). Observations pin neither model nor cost: the recording home's model is a human choice and irrlicht prices hermes from its own alias table, which has no entry for the locally configured gpt-5.6-luna (EstimateCostUSD returns 0 for an unpriced model, capacity.go:159-162) while Hermes reports estimated_cost_usd=0.0 under subscription billing; tokens_nonzero is safe because the sessions row carries input/output aggregates.

RECORD-TIME FINDINGS (2026-08-03, recording 3-2 on daemon 6ad7c28a+, coexist daemon on :7838):
(1) THE PROVISIONAL EMISSION CLAIM IS CONFIRMED. A live `delegate_task` batch of three wrote three rows into $HERMES_HOME/state.db with source='subagent' and parent_session_id = the parent id (20260803_004303_642ddd / _ae36d2 / _a3f29f -> 20260803_004253_fdd9f4), INSERTed ~5s into the parent turn WHILE the children were live (captured by a 2s store poll, not reconstructed after the fact). The store had ZERO parent_session_id rows before this run, so the assessment's alternative outcome (correct daemon=full down to incapable) is refuted by observation: daemon=full stands, and it is no longer provisional.
(2) child_birth is CORRECTED from expected_state=ready to expected_state=working. The assessment modelled the child as appearing in ready and only later going working; the recording shows the child's FIRST state_transition is `-> working` with reason "new session created". That is structural for a store adapter: the child's sessions row and its first (non-terminal) message row are INSERTed in the same scan window, so foldMessages sees a non-terminal newest row and the session is born working. The old `ready` value silently matched the child's DRAIN transition instead of its birth, which then made child_link ("at or after child_birth") unmatchable and cascaded three phases. This is a correction toward the observed truth and a strictly stronger liveness assertion, not a relaxation.
(3) THE ended_at CAVEAT IS WRONG. The assessment claimed delegate_tool never calls end_session on a child so the row's ended_at stays NULL and the subagent badge can never return to 0. The store disagrees: all three child rows carry a real ended_at (e.g. 1785710589.09172), set within ~6s of their start. Whether the dashboard badge drops is a separate question (the daemon holds a ready session whose PID is alive, and the child shares the parent PID), but the STORE-level premise of that caveat does not hold on hermes 0.19.0.
(4) The held_working floor (20000 ms) was NOT weakened. The first recording's children finished in 3-6 s, so the parent held working for only 9960 ms and the phase failed red. Per the assessment's own fourth caveat ("record should lengthen the counting tasks rather than shorten the window") the three delegated counts were widened from 30/60/90 to 250/300/350 lines and the cell was re-recorded. The window is the one the spec always asserted.
(5) tokens_nonzero STRIPPED, model PINNED — the same, already-committed hermes-column trade (see 1-6, 2-1, 2-10, 2-13). `of verify` asserts observations against the REPLAY GOLDEN summary, produced by driving core/pkg/tailer with hermes.Parser; hermes' token aggregate lives on the `sessions` row and reaches irrlicht only through ComputeMetrics, which replay never runs — so cum_input+cum_output is 0 in every hermes golden and the pin fails by construction, not by drift. The unlock is extending the #766 golden lift + StageReplayStore to hermes as #775/#776 did for antigravity. `model` is pinnable from the golden and is pinned to the live value.

text: The transient proc-<PID> presession minted by the process scanner appears in ready (hermes declares a ProcessMatcher, so this row exists before any store row does)
The REAL parent hermes session (a distinct id, shaped YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_<hex6>, from the sessions row INSERTed on the first user message) appears in ready
The user prompt drives the parent session ready -> working; the turn's only tool call is the single delegate_task batch

A delegate child appears as its own session and is born WORKING - its sessions row (source='subagent', parent_session_id = the parent's id, which the watcher's allow-list now admits) and its first non-terminal message row land in the same scan, so the fold classifies it working on the very first state_transition (reason: new session created). Recorded, not inferred.
The detector emits parent_linked binding the background child's session_id -> the parent's session_id, so SubagentCount(parent) includes the live child

The parent's own reply ('dispatched') finishes while the detached children keep running, yet the SESSION stays working - it must NOT go ready when the parent's reply ends, because hasActiveChildren still sees a working child

The background child finishes its work and its session transitions working -> ready (its last assistant row carries finish_reason='stop', which watcher.turnIsDone marks Terminal), dropping the dashboard subagent count toward 0
Only AFTER the last background child drains does the parent session transition working -> ready
